forces.title: Road construction pace slows with execution delays impacting project timelines
forces.description: India's road construction pace has significantly moderated, declining to 25 km/day in FY26 and projected to fall further to 21 km/day in FY27 from 34 km/day in FY24. Approximately Rs 1.10 lakh crore worth of under-construction Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) projects are experiencing delays exceeding nine months. These delays, stemming from heightened competitive intensity, non-availability of work fronts, and challenges in meeting construction timelines, negatively impact revenue visibility for road concession holders (asset owners/operators).
forces.source_title: Infrastructure Landscape: Vision for Viksit Bharat

forces.title: New BOT-Toll, HAM, and annuity awards expected to boost road sector activity
forces.description: The anticipated increase in Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT)-Toll, Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM), and toll-plus-annuity awards is expected to invigorate awarding activity in the roads sector. This positive trend is particularly driven by high-speed corridors and coastal connectivity projects, supported by NHAI's revised Model Concession Agreement (MCA) for BOT-Toll projects. This provides fresh opportunities for concessionaires and operators, ensuring a sustained project pipeline and future revenue streams.
forces.source_title: Infrastructure Landscape: Vision for Viksit Bharat

forces.title: Improvement in logistics performance enhances overall transport infrastructure efficiency
forces.description: India's ranking in the World Bank Logistics Performance Index improved from 44 in 2018 to 38 in 2023. This reflects significant progress in logistics competitiveness, driven by factors like integrated infrastructure ecosystems, multimodal connectivity, and efficiency. Such improvements create a more favorable environment for transport infrastructure operators (roads, railways, ports) by ensuring smoother and more reliable movement of goods, potentially increasing throughput and utilization of their assets.
forces.source_title: Infrastructure Landscape: Vision for Viksit Bharat

forces.title: High budgetary allocation and asset monetization drive infrastructure investment
forces.description: The Union Budget 2026–27 increased capital investment outlay for infrastructure to Rs. 12.22 lakh crore (US$ 138.3 billion), an 11.5% rise. Concurrently, the Second Asset Monetization Plan aims to reinvest Rs. 10 lakh crore (US$ 115.34 billion) in new projects from 2025-30. This substantial government commitment, coupled with asset recycling, fuels opportunities for transport infrastructure asset owners and operators, attracting private participation and ensuring continued development and upgrades.

forces.title: Increasing private investment in roads, driven by BOT model revival and MoRTH reforms
forces.description: Private investment in India's highway sector is projected to reach nearly Rs. 1 lakh crore (US$ 11.32 billion) in FY2026–27, spurred by the revival of the Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) model. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) revised the BOT bidding framework, allowing institutional investors direct participation, further boosting private capital. This significant inflow of private funds directly benefits road concession holders by facilitating new project development and expanding operational assets.

forces.title: Growing PPP model adoption and allocated capex for rail infrastructure expansion
forces.description: Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) are becoming critical for railway infrastructure development, with 18 projects worth Rs. 166.9 billion completed and 7 projects worth Rs. 163.6 billion under implementation. The Union Budget 2026–27 allocated a record capital expenditure of Rs. 2,93,030 crore (US$ 33.16 billion) to Indian Railways. This focus on PPPs and substantial capital outlay creates significant opportunities for private players in rail track ownership, metro development, and station redevelopment, supporting long-term growth for rail infrastructure operators.

forces.title: High Vande Bharat occupancy reflects strong passenger rail demand and utilization
forces.description: The average occupancy of Vande Bharat trains during 2025-26 reached approximately 100%. This high utilization rate indicates robust demand for modern, premium passenger rail services. For rail infrastructure owners and operators, sustained high occupancy translates into consistent revenue streams and validates investments in upgrading passenger rail networks and rolling stock. It signals a positive outlook for the financial viability and expansion of advanced rail services.

forces.title: One Nation One Port Process streamlines operations and reduces logistics costs
forces.description: The 'One Nation One Port Process' (ONOP) initiative, launched in February 2025, aims to unify documentation and processes across all major Indian ports. This has already reduced paperwork by 33% for container and 29% for bulk cargo operations, leading to substantial savings in logistics costs. For port operators, this streamlining enhances operational efficiency, reduces turnaround times, and improves overall competitiveness, contributing to higher throughput and better profitability.

forces.title: Strong growth in core industries drives demand for freight across transport modes
forces.description: Key core infrastructure industries like steel (9.53% YoY growth) and cement (8.71% YoY growth) recorded robust performance in FY26. This strong output from heavy industries directly translates into increased demand for freight transport across roads, railways, and ports. For transport infrastructure asset owners and operators, this signifies higher cargo volumes, leading to increased utilization of freight corridors, port handling capacity, and road networks, thereby boosting throughput-based revenues.

forces.title: Maritime decarbonization initiatives drive transition to green ports and cleaner shipping
forces.description: India is committing to net-zero emissions by 2070, reinforcing this through the 'Conference on Maritime Decarbonization in India' and initiatives like 'Harit Sagar' and 'Harit Nauka' guidelines. Plans include establishing a green, digital corridor with the Port of Rotterdam for green hydrogen export. This represents a significant structural shift for port operators, requiring investments in green infrastructure, sustainable technologies, and operational changes, potentially reshaping capital expenditure and long-term operating models to comply with environmental mandates and leverage new energy solutions.

forces.title: Road network upgrade and expansion plans present massive long-term investment opportunities
forces.description: India is embarking on ambitious plans to upgrade 25,000 km of two-lane highways to four lanes at a cost of Rs. 10 lakh crore (US$ 117 billion) and expand 16,000 km of four-lane highways to six lanes for Rs. 6 lakh crore (US$ 69.93 billion). These projects, with detailed reports under preparation, are expected to commence by 2027. This signifies a massive long-term investment pipeline for road infrastructure asset owners and operators, ensuring sustained growth in concession and annuity revenues over the coming decades.

forces.title: Multimodal logistics parks development enhances road freight efficiency and traffic
forces.description: The government is developing 35 multimodal logistics parks under Bharatmala Pariyojana, with an investment of Rs. 46,000 crore (US$ 5.21 billion), aiming to handle around 700 million metric tonnes of cargo. These parks are designed to integrate various transport modes, improving logistics efficiency and reducing costs. For road and highway operators, these developments are a significant tailwind, as they are expected to consolidate and streamline freight movement, leading to increased traffic volumes and sustained revenue generation on connecting road networks.

viewpoints.title: Transport Infrastructure is central to India's Viksit Bharat 2047 vision
viewpoints.description: CareEdge views infrastructure development, particularly transport, as a defining moment for India's transformation into a developed, inclusive, and globally competitive economy by 2047. Sustained public capital expenditure and an integrated ecosystem approach, focusing on multimodal connectivity and logistics efficiency, underscore this positive outlook. This strategic emphasis on infrastructure creates a multiplier effect across various sectors, attracting private investment and reshaping economic geography.
viewpoints.source_title: Infrastructure Landscape: Vision for Viksit Bharat

viewpoints.title: Stable outlook for Indian roads despite execution challenges and monetization moderation
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings maintains a stable outlook for India's roads infrastructure segment. This stability is driven by resilient annuity and toll cash flows from an expanding base of operational assets. However, the sector faces short-term headwinds, including a slowdown in the construction pace and moderation in the monetization of Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) projects, indicating persistent execution challenges.
viewpoints.source_title: Infrastructure Landscape: Vision for Viksit Bharat

viewpoints.title: India's port sector activity is set for growth with increasing trade and private participation
viewpoints.description: IBEF projects a positive trajectory for India's port infrastructure, driven by robust increases in international trade volumes, which account for 95% of the country's trade by volume. The growing involvement of the private sector in port infrastructure development is also a key factor supporting this expansion. Strategic initiatives and government support further enhance port activity and capacity.

demand_drivers.description: Consumers' growing preference for fresh produce and packaged foods necessitates robust cold chain logistics.
Online retail drives demand for efficient, temperature-controlled delivery networks for food products.

new_opportunities.description: The need for refrigerated container storage and cargo handling facilities at transport hubs increases due to cold chain market growth, creating opportunities for port/airport operators.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Temperature-controlled infrastructure at ports and airports

market_sizing.methodology: Reported market size for India's cold chain market. Growth factors include increasing demand for perishable goods, e-commerce expansion, and government infrastructure initiatives (e.g., PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana).
market_sizing.source_title: Ensuring food safety and regulatory compliance in warehousing and distribution

demand_drivers.description: Sustained government capital expenditure and focus on expanding the National Highway network.

market_sizing.methodology: The National Highway (NH) network length expanded to approximately 1.47 lakh km by FY26 from 1.00 lakh km in FY16. This growth is driven by government focus on expanding road infrastructure.
market_sizing.source_title: Infrastructure Landscape: Vision for Viksit Bharat

demand_drivers.description: Union Budget allocations directly fund highway development and operational aspects handled by NHAI.

market_sizing.methodology: Budgetary allocation to the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) for the specified fiscal year. This funding supports the development and maintenance of national highways.

demand_drivers.description: Government's push to recycle capital by monetizing operational infrastructure assets, attracting private investment.

market_sizing.methodology: Funds raised by NHAI through the InvIT mode during FY26. InvITs are investment vehicles for monetizing infrastructure assets.

demand_drivers.description: Rapid urban growth and development of smart cities drive the need for efficient public transit systems like metros.

new_opportunities.description: Significant government plans to expand metro networks across many cities, creating long-term opportunities for rail infrastructure owners and operators.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Development of new metro rail corridors

market_sizing.methodology: Government target for Metro rail network expansion across 100 cities by 2047.

demand_drivers.description: Increased movement of people across the country supported by network expansion.

market_sizing.methodology: Total number of passengers carried by Indian Railways. Conversion from 'crore' to 'billion' (1 crore = 10 million).

demand_drivers.description: Strong growth in key industrial commodities like fertilisers, pig iron & steel, iron ore, and containers drives demand for rail freight.

market_sizing.methodology: Freight loading on Indian Railways. The figure crossed 1,700 MMT in FY26, up from 1,614.90 MMT in FY25.

demand_drivers.description: Continued governmental emphasis on expanding and upgrading India's rail network to enhance capacity and connectivity.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected investment in rail infrastructure. This represents a substantial capital outlay for track owners and metro infrastructure.

demand_drivers.description: Strong performance in industrial commodities freight loading drives a significant portion of railway revenue.
Increasing demand for rail-based mobility contributes to passenger earnings.

market_sizing.methodology: Gross revenue of Indian Railways, reflecting earnings from both freight and passenger segments.

demand_drivers.description: Higher movement of key industrial commodities such as steel, cement, fertilizers, and containers contributes significantly to freight earnings.

market_sizing.methodology: Freight revenue of Indian Railways, identified as the primary revenue driver for the sector, accounting for 63.97% of total receipts.

demand_drivers.description: India's growing share in global trade drives the need for expanded port capacity to handle cargo.

market_sizing.methodology: Combined cargo handling capacity of major and non-major ports in India, which almost doubled between 2014 and 2025.

demand_drivers.description: Increased export activities directly translate to higher cargo volumes passing through ports.
Overall increase in India's international trade drives port cargo traffic.

market_sizing.methodology: Total cargo traffic handled by all major ports in India. This indicates the throughput for port operators.

demand_drivers.description: The volume of goods traded internationally and domestically via sea routes directly impacts port throughput.

market_sizing.methodology: Breakdown of cargo handled by major ports, with overseas cargo representing 76.67% and coastal cargo 23.33% of the total.

demand_drivers.driver: Viksit Bharat vision and economic growth
demand_drivers.description: Long-term national vision for economic development and increasing trade necessitates massive expansion of port capacity.
Government's flagship program for port-led development, driving investment and capacity enhancement.

market_sizing.methodology: Government target for port handling capacity under the Sagarmala program by 2047, supported by Rs. 80 lakh crore (US$ 903.65 billion) investments.

demand_drivers.description: Robust growth in India's international trade directly drives container movement through ports.

market_sizing.methodology: Container traffic in India at major ports, measured in Million TEUs (Twenty-foot Equivalent Units).

demand_drivers.description: Government's focus on developing inland waterways as sustainable transport arteries to complement road and rail networks.

market_sizing.methodology: Cargo movement volume on India's Inland Waterways, recorded by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI).

demand_drivers.description: Shift in cargo traffic from major to non-major ports, driven by strategic location and evolving trade patterns.
Slight increase in overseas and coastal cargo handled by non-major ports.

market_sizing.methodology: Total cargo traffic handled by non-major ports in India, which accounted for 45.14% of total traffic in FY26.
